info.name: CYCLES_LIGHT_SKY
info.comment: Cycles vendor extension: 'sky' light subtype, a physically-based procedural sun+sky dome (Cycles SkyTextureNode, Nishita multiple-scattering model) that drives the scene background exactly like an 'hdri' light -- no HDRI image required. The dome is evaluated in world space with world +Z up; the horizon is the world XY plane and instance transforms do not reorient it. A world should contain at most one background-type light ('hdri' or 'sky'): Cycles has a single background slot, so only the first one found is used and any others are ignored with a warning. 'visible'=false shows the renderer 'background' to camera rays while the sky keeps illuminating the scene.

objects.name: sky
objects.description: procedural sun+sky dome light (Nishita atmosphere model)

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: tint multiplied into the whole sky dome (sun disc included)

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: whether camera rays see the sky dome; when false they see the renderer 'background' instead while the sky keeps illuminating the scene

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: overall intensity scale of the sky dome (sun disc included)

parameters.name: sunDirection
parameters.description: world-space direction pointing toward the sun (need not be normalized); z is 'up' -- negative z puts the sun below the horizon

parameters.name: sunDisc
parameters.description: render the sun disc itself in the sky dome

parameters.name: sunSize
parameters.description: apparent (full) angular diameter of the sun disc in radians; default is the real sun (~0.545 degrees)

parameters.name: sunIntensity
parameters.description: multiplier on the sun disc's contribution

parameters.name: altitude
parameters.description: altitude of the viewpoint above sea level in meters

parameters.name: airDensity
parameters.description: relative density of air molecules (Rayleigh scattering); higher values give a bluer sky

parameters.name: dustDensity
parameters.description: relative density of dust and water droplets (Mie scattering); higher values give a hazier sky

parameters.name: ozoneDensity
parameters.description: relative density of the ozone layer; higher values make the sky bluer around sunrise/sunset
